objective.text: Assess the trust boundary created by ignoring a query parameter during signature validation.

difficulty.rationale: Identify which data remains authenticated after an explicit signature exclusion.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

stem: An export link signs the account path but ignores the query parameter format during validation. The UI currently sends format=csv. Which review comment correctly describes the security boundary?

options.text: Treat format as caller-controlled and validate it against allowed formats; the signature does not protect its value.
options.rationale: An ignored parameter can be changed while the signature remains valid, so its value needs independent validation.

options.text: Reject every link with format because ignored parameters always invalidate signatures.
options.rationale: Ignoring a parameter intentionally permits it to vary without invalidating the signature.
options.misconception: Ignoring a parameter intentionally permits it to vary without invalidating the signature.

options.text: Treat format as trusted because the account path is signed.
options.rationale: Authenticating the path does not authenticate a query parameter explicitly excluded from verification.
options.misconception: Authenticating the path does not authenticate a query parameter explicitly excluded from verification.

options.text: Use the presence of a signature as authorization for any account ID supplied in the body.
options.rationale: The signed URL authenticates only its covered data and does not authenticate unrelated request body values.
options.misconception: The signed URL authenticates only its covered data and does not authenticate unrelated request body values.
